definitions.explanation: Something that cannot be understood or explained through normal reasoning. Often describes phenomena or events that defy logical explanation.
A mysterious occurrence or thing worthy of wonder.

examples.japanese: {不可思議|ふかしぎ}な{体験|たいけん}をした。
{宇宙|うちゅう}には{不可思議|ふかしぎ}なことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many inexplicable things in the universe.

examples.japanese: {世界|せかい}の{七|なな}{不可思議|ふかしぎ}を{巡|めぐ}る{旅|たび}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: I set off on a journey to visit the Seven Wonders of the World.

notes:
COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
{不|ふ} (not) + {可|か} (possible) + {思議|しぎ} (to fathom/comprehend)

Literally "not possible to comprehend" - beyond the reach of thought or reason.

BUDDHIST ORIGIN:
Originally a Buddhist term referring to the ineffable nature of enlightenment and divine mysteries that transcend human understanding.

GRAMMAR:
・{不可思議|ふかしぎ}な + noun - mysterious ~
・{不可思議|ふかしぎ}に{思|おも}う - to find mysterious
・〜は{不可思議|ふかしぎ}だ - ~ is inexplicable

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{世界|せかい}の{七|なな}{不可思議|ふかしぎ} - Seven Wonders of the World
・{不可思議|ふかしぎ}な{現象|げんしょう} - mysterious phenomenon
・{不可思議|ふかしぎ}な{出来事|できごと} - inexplicable event

NUANCE:
Stronger than {不思議|ふしぎ} (strange, mysterious). {不可思議|ふかしぎ} implies something truly beyond human comprehension, while {不思議|ふしぎ} can be used for everyday curiosities.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{不思議|ふしぎ} - strange, mysterious (more common, lighter)
・{神秘的|しんぴてき} - mystical
・{謎|なぞ} - mystery, riddle
・{怪奇|かいき} - bizarre, weird

REGISTER:
Slightly formal/literary. Often used in dramatic or philosophical contexts.
